label: words repair
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: airplane
Length: 60 s: 200-235 words in all, one sentence per beat (15 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 218 words in all, about 15 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 235 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- Older Cessna 172s, such as the 172R, have a maximum takeoff weight of about 2,450 lb (1,111 kg); newer 172S models are certified to 2,550 lb (1,157 kg).
- A Cessna 172 rotates at about 55 knots indicated airspeed, roughly 100 km/h.

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: wings pop onto the white tube on the runway. actions: plane show; plane wingsOn (on "wings")
   idea: two wings on a tube make an airplane
   cue words: "wings"
2. problem
   on screen: the wheels spin on the runway but the plane stays pinned under yellow weight arrows. actions: weight show (on "sits"); plane rollWheels (on "turn")
   idea: flat wings give no lift, so it sits on the runway
   cue words: "sits", "turn"
3. stakes
   on screen: the weight counter ticks up to 2450 and its bar fills red. actions: plane rollWheelsBack (on "Cessna"); pole 1 show (on "Cessna"); w count show (on "Cessna"); w count count
   idea: an older Cessna 172 weighs about 2,450 pounds, all pinned down
   cue words: "Cessna", "2,450"
   its fact: Older Cessna 172s, such as the 172R, have a maximum takeoff weight of about 2,450 lb (1,111 kg); newer 172S models are certified to 2,550 lb (1,157 kg).
4. fix1
   on screen: an engine and a spinning propeller appear on the nose, and white air streams straight past the flat wing. actions: w count hide (on "So"); weight hide (on "So"); plane engineOn (on "engine"); plane spinProp (on "propeller"); air flat show (on "air"); air stream start (on "air")
   idea: an engine and propeller push air, but it slides past flat wings
   cue words: "So", "engine", "propeller", "air"
5. fix2
   on screen: the wing top bulges, fast air arrows run over it and yellow lift arrows rise. actions: air flat hide (on "So"); air stream stop (on "So"); plane curve (on "curve"); air fast show (on "speeds"); lift show (on "lifts")
   idea: a curved wing top speeds the air up and lifts
   cue words: "So", "curve", "speeds", "lifts"
6. fix3
   on screen: a fin and a stabilizer pop onto the tail. actions: air fast hide (on "But"); lift hide (on "But"); plane tailOn (on "tail")
   idea: a tail with a fin and stabilizer keeps the nose straight
   cue words: "But", "tail"
7. fix4
   on screen: the yellow rudder swings sideways and the yellow elevator tilts up on their hinges. actions: plane steer (on "rudder"); plane elevate (on "elevator")
   idea: a hinged rudder and elevator steer the nose
   cue words: "rudder", "elevator"
8. name
   on screen: a yellow outline traces the whole plane. actions: plane steerBack; plane elevateBack; plane outline show
   idea: this is an airplane
   cue words: (none)
9. name2
   on screen: a yellow outline traces the curved wing. actions: plane outline hide; wing outline show
   idea: the curved wing shape is an airfoil
   cue words: (none)
10. how
   on screen: the plane rolls down the runway and climbs off it while the speed counter ticks to 100. actions: wing outline hide; pole 2 show; speed show; speed count (on "100"); plane rollWheels; plane takeoff
   idea: at about 100 km/h the wings lift it off
   cue words: "100"
   its fact: A Cessna 172 rotates at about 55 knots indicated airspeed, roughly 100 km/h.
11. problem2
   on screen: a gust pushes down one wing and the plane tips onto its side in the air. actions: speed hide (on "But"); gust arrows show (on "gust"); plane gust (on "tips")
   idea: a gust tips it onto its side
   cue words: "But", "gust", "tips"
12. problem3
   on screen: beside the tipped plane in the air, a speed gauge climbs to 100 and turns red. actions: pole 2 show (on "And"); land speed show (on "And"); land speed count
   idea: to land it must slow, but 100 km/h is too fast
   cue words: "And"
13. fix5
   on screen: flaps appear and tilt down, the plane levels out and settles back onto the runway. actions: land speed hide (on "So"); gust arrows hide (on "So"); plane flapsOn (on "flaps"); plane gustBack (on "level"); plane flaps (on "slow"); plane takeoffBack (on "slow")
   idea: flaps level it and slow it onto the runway
   cue words: "So", "flaps", "level", "slow"
14. finish
   on screen: a blue door and big windows pop onto the fuselage and stairs appear under the door. actions: plane spinPropBack (on "Add"); plane rollWheelsBack (on "Add"); plane flapsBack (on "Add"); plane doorOn (on "door"); plane windowsOn (on "windows"); stairs show (on "stairs")
   idea: a door, windows and stairs complete it
   cue words: "Add", "door", "windows", "stairs"
15. congrats
   on screen: the finished build, calm
   idea: an airplane
   cue words: (none)

Your narration below has problems the free checks found. Fix every one and return the whole narration again.

- fix "But now the nose wanders, so you add a tail with a…" does not solve "now the nose wanders": say how it stops that very problem

Your narration:
hook: If you bolt two wings onto a tube, you have an airplane.
problem: But the flat wings give no lift, so the wheels turn and the plane sits on the runway.
stakes: An older Cessna 172 weighs about 2,450 pounds, and gravity pins every pound of it down.
fix1: So you add an engine and a propeller, but the air just slides past the flat wings.
fix2: So you curve the top of the wing, and the air speeds up over it and the wing lifts.
fix3: But now the nose wanders, so you add a tail with a fin and a stabilizer that hold it straight.
fix4: Then you hinge the back of the tail, so the rudder swings the nose sideways and the elevator tilts it up.
name: This is an airplane.
name2: The curved wing shape is called an airfoil.
how: At about 100 kilometers per hour, the air over the wings lifts the plane off the runway.
problem2: But a gust of wind pushes one wing down, and the plane tips onto its side.
problem3: And to land, the plane must slow down, but at 100 kilometers per hour it is far too fast.
fix5: So you add flaps on the wings that level the plane and slow it until it settles onto the runway.
finish: Add a door, windows and stairs so people can board.
congrats: Congratulations, you have built an airplane.
